title: Nonoperative Treatment for Injuries to the In-Season Throwing Shoulder: A Current Concepts Review With Clinical Commentary
authors: Stone MA, Jalali O, Alluri RK, et al.
population: Overhead throwing athletes; baseball-specific rehabilitation discussion.
access: Free full text verified and read; official NIH article HTML retrieved on 2026-10-12.
findings: Describes an examination-led, phased progression from symptom management and capacity restoration to throwing. Considers the entire kinetic chain and athlete context.
limitations: Level 5 clinical commentary; proposed phases and numerical criteria are not a prospectively validated clearance algorithm. Published protocols are examples, not universal prescriptions.

title: National Athletic Trainers’ Association Position Statement: Evaluation, Management, and Outcomes of and Return-to-Play Criteria for Overhead Athletes With Superior Labral Anterior-Posterior Injuries
authors: Michener LA, Abrams JS, Huxel Bliven KC, et al.
type: Position statement informed by systematic evidence review and expert consensus
population: Overhead athletes with SLAP injuries; studies include baseball and other populations.
access: Free full text verified and read; official NIH article HTML retrieved on 2026-10-12.
findings: Explains the biceps-labral complex, limitations of isolated diagnostic findings, first-line nonoperative management and limitations of return-to-play evidence.
limitations: Many recommendations have limited or inconsistent research support; published in 2018. Imaging findings must be interpreted with symptoms and examination, and surgical recommendations need current specialist context.

title: Management of Common Upper Extremity Injuries in Throwing Athletes: A Critical Review of Current Outcomes
authors: Maier J, Oak SR, Soloff L, Schickendantz M, Frangiamore S
population: Overhead throwers, including professional and collegiate baseball players.
access: Free full text verified and read; official NIH article HTML retrieved on 2026-10-12.
findings: Discusses SLAP, instability, cuff and other shoulder injuries; distinguishes return to play from restoration of prior performance and describes position-dependent outcomes.
limitations: Largely observational surgical literature with varying definitions and selection effects. Treatment groups and procedures cannot be ranked as if randomized.

title: Nonoperative Management of Ulnar Collateral Ligament Injuries in the Throwing Athlete: A Framework for Return to Throwing
authors: Wyatt PB, Vanderkwaak B, Brown R, Goodloe JB

title: Return-to-Sport Criteria After Upper Extremity Surgery in Athletes—A Scoping Review, Part 2: Ulnar Collateral Ligament of the Elbow Procedures
authors: Griffith R, Bolia IK, Fretes N, et al.
population: 14 studies and 1,335 athletes after UCL surgery; predominantly reconstruction.
access: Free full text verified and read; official NIH article HTML retrieved on 2026-10-12.
findings: Time was reported in every included study, while functional measures were less often described. The review identifies inadequate reporting and validation of return criteria.
limitations: Cannot determine whether criteria were absent in practice or merely underreported. Heterogeneous procedures and populations; no comparison validates one clearance battery.
license: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. Link to the full paper; original teaching summaries only.

title: Management of Ulnar Collateral Ligament Injuries of the Elbow
authors: Ryan PM, Beyer J, Hartman H, Ismail H, Alam M, DeFroda SF

title: Hamstring Strain Injury Rehabilitation
authors: Hickey JT, Opar DA, Weiss LJ, Heiderscheit BC
type: Current clinical concepts / narrative evidence review
population: Athletes with hamstring strains, drawing heavily on running and field-sport evidence.
access: Free full text verified and read; official NIH article HTML retrieved on 2026-10-12.
findings: Integrates progressive running, knee-flexor and hip-extensor loading, symptom monitoring and psychological readiness; explicitly discusses limits of reinjury prediction.

title: Management of Proximal Hamstring Injuries: Non-operative and Operative Treatment
authors: Yetter TR, Halvorson RT, Wong SE, Harris JD, Allahabadi S
population: Elite and recreational patients with proximal hamstring injuries; not exclusively baseball.

title: No Difference in Patient-Reported Outcomes Between Operative and Non-operative Management of Proximal Hamstring Injuries, but Return to Sports Is Higher in Operative Treatment: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis
authors: Thamrongskulsiri N, Limskul D, Tanpowpong T, Kuptniratsaikul S, Ranawat AS, Itthipanichpong T
type: Systematic review and meta-analysis of comparative studies
population: Predominantly active, middle-aged recreational patients with proximal hamstring tendon avulsions.
access: Free full text verified and read; official NIH article HTML retrieved on 2026-10-12.
findings: Pooled patient-reported outcomes were similar, while return to preinjury sport favored surgery. Authors emphasize population and selection limitations.
limitations: Mostly nonrandomized evidence with selection bias and heterogeneity; results cannot be directly transferred to elite baseball. Reported denominators vary across outcomes; no pooled success percentage is used in these lessons.
locations: Results: Return to Sports at Pre-injury Performance Level
